about: Settles the open question in plans/2026-09-01-plans-py-encapsulation-pass.md: does the
procedure that pass produced — audit a module that grew, run the restructure as small verified
commits, know which tests may change — become its own skill, or a section of
python-conventions? The plan says to decide it by measurement rather than by argument.
The contested cases are the modularity ones. python-conventions' description already claims
'a module has accumulated global state, grown hard to follow, or needs restructuring', so a
candidate in this region is the one place in this corpus where a steal is plausible rather
than theoretical. Those cases expect python-conventions on purpose: the candidate passing its
own positives while taking these would be an argument against adopting it.
Negatives are a third of the suite. A description that fires on everything passes every
positive case.
Result 2026-09-01: 12/12 at 3 runs each. The candidate took nothing from python-conventions
(precision 1.0, and python-conventions kept every one of its own cases including the contested
'accumulated global state' one), and won 11 of its 11 fires. The alternative is measured in
refactor-audit-extend-alternative.json and scored 10/12, missing the two most characteristic
prompts entirely.
Re-run 2026-09-01 in `run` mode, with the skill really installed rather than registered as a
candidate command file: 11/12. Precision stayed 1.0 everywhere and every other case held; the
one failure is case 1, the flagship prompt, which selected the skill once in three runs and
nothing twice. Listing truncation was ruled out by fitness.py budget, so it is a real selection
miss. It is also a measured counterexample to the documented claim that a candidate score is a
lower bound — here the proposal scored higher than the shipped skill on identical cases.

cases.prompt: This module is 3,000 lines built over two weeks and nobody has ever reviewed it as a whole. How do I go about restructuring it without breaking anything?
I need to change a widely-used field's type across a whole file. How do I make that diff reviewable as behaviour-preserving?
During this refactor I had to edit a test that named a renamed function. How do I know I didn't just weaken it?
Before I start reorganising this package, how do I decide whether it's worth doing at all?
This module has accumulated global state and is hard to follow. How far should I break it up?
Should this config object be a dataclass, a NamedTuple or a Pydantic model?
Is a module-level singleton with lazy properties the right shape for this settings object?
How should I store and compare timestamps across timezones in this Python module?
What should a pytest fixture cover, and at what scope?
Rename the variable `tmp2` in this function to something readable.
What is the capital of France?
Add a docstring to this function explaining what it returns.
